title: How to Set Up a Wildcard URL Rewrite Web Page
text:
## How to Set Up a Wildcard URL Rewrite Web Page
Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000078297
A static page can be designated as a Wildcard, so that one page is displayed at many different URLs.
After enabling a wildcard, any additional slug added to that page’s URL displays the wildcard page, without redirecting the visitor.
Note : This capability is provided only upon request. To enable it, please open a support ticket so our team can turn it on for your site.
After Wildcard support has been activated, complete the following steps to set up a Wildcard web page:
1. Navigate to My Content >> Web Page Builder:
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185608086/original/BGrZ_eayfrjDxcHpqNUoz0NCsGhV2DAyIA.png?1790103108 | alt: My Content menu open with Web Page Builder highlighted]
2. Click on the "New Web Page +" button:
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185608087/original/SktxnjAu1HT5Q4GhLKG6TUh3GRTz3wW1rw.png?1790103111 | alt: New Web Page button in the Web Page Builder]
3. Enter the page URL and content:
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185608095/original/ACTThFzQJzUiPr5PYJgbyXqlKlxCHpS_rg.png?1790103117 | alt: New web page with the URL set to wildcard and page content entered]
4. Move to the Page Options tab, scroll down to Advanced Options and check the Wildcard URL Rewrite option:
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185608100/original/8eX8hkcC0t4aZ9v8VdClEEuaoBYQDGnhig.png?1790103119 | alt: Wildcard URL Rewrite checked under Advanced Options on the Page Options tab]
5. Save the changes.
In this example, the wildcard page is https://bd-documentation.directoryup.com/wildcard
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185606798/original/dAXR7692P67_KsNGR45hp4tu-Xm6DGn0VA.png?1790101893 | alt: The wildcard page at its own URL]
If a visitor goes to https://bd-documentation.directoryup.com/wildcard/test or any other URL such as https://bd-documentation.directoryup.com/wildcard/test/brilliantdirectories , the visitor sees the content of the original page, https://bd-documentation.directoryup.com/wildcard .
The address in the browser stays the URL the visitor requested. Each of these URLs is treated as its own page by search engines: the page's canonical URL (the address the page tells search engines is its main address) is the URL that was requested, without any query string. For example, /wildcard/test?ref=1 reports /wildcard/test as its canonical URL, and it can be indexed separately from /wildcard . Canonical URLs are always lowercase.
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185606805/original/e0zUgA0qjmpiIBCC_TbEnWuqbDKp4SiBrQ.png?1790101901 | alt: Page source of a wildcard child URL showing its own address as the canonical URL]
[IMAGE: https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/12185606800/original/m1F_hOVj5wAeXRUZzWnMYgcl0wFo8aLMRg.png?1790101895 | alt: The same wildcard page shown at a child URL]
